evals.prompt: My Cronbach's alpha is 0.82 for my 8-item motivation scale, so the scale is good to use, right?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-measurement-gate: explains that alpha assumes tau-equivalence (equal loadings) and is only a lower bound, so it asks for McDonald's omega alongside alpha and a dimensionality check, and stresses that internal consistency is not evidence of validity. Does not bless the scale on alpha alone.

assertions.value: Refuses to treat a single alpha as sufficient; requires omega (or a stated tau-equivalence caveat) and separates reliability from validity.

evals.prompt: My anxiety questionnaire has excellent internal consistency, so that proves it's a valid measure of anxiety, doesn't it?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-measurement-gate and corrects the reliability=validity conflation: high consistency only means items move together, not that they capture the intended construct. Requires separate validity evidence (content, criterion, convergent/discriminant construct validity).

assertions.value: States that reliability does not establish validity and enumerates the distinct validity evidence required.

evals.prompt: I built a new 6-item measure of teacher burnout. How do I show it actually works before I use it in my study?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-measurement-gate: lays out the validation program — define the construct, content validity, dimensionality/CFA, reliability with omega, and criterion/convergent/discriminant construct validity — and routes the factor-model execution to the psychometrics skill.

assertions.value: Prescribes construct definition + dimensionality + reliability (omega) + multiple validity evidences, not just an alpha.

evals.prompt: I want to compare mean trust in government across three countries using the same 5-item scale. Can I just compare the group averages?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-measurement-gate: requires measurement invariance testing (configural -> metric -> scalar multi-group CFA) before comparing latent means, warning that without at least scalar invariance a group difference may be a measurement artifact rather than a real difference.

evals.prompt: I'm writing a brand-new questionnaire. Help me word the items and choose the response-scale anchors for each question.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-survey-design. Writing and wording items and choosing response scales is instrument construction, upstream of measurement validation.

evals.prompt: I already trust my scale. Just compute the mean and standard deviation of the total score for me.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statistical-analysis for descriptive computation. There is no measurement-quality question to gate here.
